unstated_means: these passages do not state it
kind_year: a calendar year with four digits
not_an_option: Your "entry" {given!r} is no number of "list". Answer with a number from "list", 0 if no entry fits.
name_not_listed: Your "entry" {given!r} is no number of "list". Answer with a number from "list", "new" if the name is none of its entries, or 0 if the words name no such thing.
wrong_type: Your "value" {given!r} is not {wrong}. Answer with {wrong}, exactly as the passage writes it.
quote_not_in_source: Your "quote" stands in none of the sources shown. Copy a passage character for character from "sources" or from the "quote" of the row itself.
quote_not_in_passage: Your "quote" stands neither in "source", nor in the heading of its section, nor in "around". Copy it character for character from one of them.
quote_too_short: Your "quote" is too short to name a place (at least {minimum} characters). Quote the whole sentence or the whole line the answer stands in.
answer_not_in_quote: Your "quote" does not contain {answer!r}. If it prints another word of the document for this, write that word character for character under "value_raw"; otherwise quote the place where the answer really stands.
answer_not_in_quote_text: Your "quote" does not contain {answer!r}. Write the answer as your quote prints it, character for character, or quote the place where it really stands.
or_unstated: If it stands nowhere, answer with "{unstated}".
shape_rule: Output ONLY the JSON object, on ONE line, with no text before or after it, no code fence, no <think> block and no second object. Quotation marks INSIDE a quote must be escaped as \" — if that is tedious, shorten the quote to a place without quotation marks.
cut_off: Your answer was cut off after {limit} tokens and is therefore not a complete JSON object.
shorter: Answer more briefly: quote only the short place where the field stands.
shorter_frame: Answer with fewer pairs and quote only the short place where the scenario or the year stands.
shorter_rows: Answer with fewer tuples and quote only the short place where the value stands.
compute_needs_code: A number without code has no evidence. Work it out with the action object, or answer with "value": null.
compute_taken: {label} now stands under "numbers", and in the code as numbers["{label}"].
compute_not_taken: The number under "take" was not taken: {reason}. Copy its quote character for character from the passage shown that holds it, with the number in it.
compute_quote: Your "quote" does not stand in the passage of {label}. Copy from that passage, character for character, what {label} is.
compute_rejected: The number under "value" was not taken: {reason}. Give it as a number, exactly as the code printed it, and under "used" the numbers the code worked it out from.
value_in_several_rows: The "quote" of these numbers runs over several table rows and prints the number on more than one of them: {values}. Give only these entries again, each with the one row it stands in as its "quote".
not_an_address: This does not say your value is wrong: check its quote, the line its address names. The address {at!r} names no line or cell of what you were shown. Give the address as it stands before the line: its number, a letter before it where the block has one, and in a line that "|" divides a point and the number of the cell.
words_not_in_line: This does not say your value is wrong: check its quote, the line its address names. The words {words!r} do not stand in the line {at!r} names, or they name more than one number. Give the address of the line that prints them and the words of exactly one value as that line prints them.
not_an_address_quote: This does not say your value is wrong: check its quote. The quote {quote!r} names no line of what you were shown. Give under "quote" the line as it was shown, character for character, without the address before it.
words_not_in_line_quote: This does not say your value is wrong: check its quote. The words {words!r} do not stand in the line {quote!r}, or they name more than one number. Give under "quote" the line that prints them, character for character, and the words of exactly one value as that line prints them.
shorter_field: Put rows with the same answer together in "groups" and quote only the short place where the field stands.
shorter_review: Quote only the short place where the field stands, and leave out every field the two passages do not carry.
reasoning_only: You only thought and answered nothing: your reply was empty. Do not think ahead, output the result directly.
no_object: Your answer contained no JSON object at all.
syntax: Your JSON breaks at character {position} ({message}), at this place: {around!r}.
outside_text: There was text beside the JSON object: {extra!r}.
not_an_object: Your answer was a {kind} structure and not a JSON object.
key_not_a_list: In your answer "{key}" was not a list.
wrong_shape: Your answer did not have the form that was asked for.
code_failed: The code did not run: {error}. Answer now without a calculation, or correct the code.
code_silent: The code ran but printed nothing. Print every result with print(), or answer without a calculation.
